info.name: DEPLOYTOUR local MVD
info.description:
Every API of the local Minimum Viable Dataspace deployed with ging_deploy/deploy-local-mvd.sh (kind, http://localhost).

1 · Walkthrough: run the folder in order (Run collection / newman). Each request stores the ids the next ones need
(offers, negotiation, agreement, transfer, EDR token) in collection variables, and polling requests repeat until the process finishes.
2–6 · Reference: every endpoint per API. They reuse the ids captured by the walkthrough, so run it once first.

No authentication on any API. The ingress only routes Host: localhost. See ging_deploy/postman/README.md.

item.name: B · Publishing (provider)
item.description:
Two entries on the provider: `pm-data-<runId>` (only the participant named "consumer" may contract it) and
`pm-nobody-<runId>` (a rule nobody satisfies). Each entry = asset + policy definition + contract definition.

request.description: Asset = public properties + private data address (where the provider's data plane fetches the data). Returns IdResponse {@id, createdAt}.
ODRL policy: active membership AND the MembershipCredential's `name` claim equals `consumer` (checked at negotiation time). Returns IdResponse with the generated id.
Offers the asset (selected by id) under the policy: access policy = who sees it, contract policy = what the agreement requires.
Second asset, for the rejected negotiation.
Requires name = nobody: no participant satisfies it.
Offers the nobody asset.

item.name: C · Discovery
item.description: The consumer asks its own control plane to fetch the provider's catalog over DSP. The test script stores the offers for the next folder.

item.name: C1 Consumer requests the provider catalog

request.description: Returns a DCAT catalog: one dataset per asset this consumer may see, each with `hasPolicy` (the ODRL offer) and `distribution` (transfer types). The offers are saved, with `assigner` and `target` added, as `offerData` / `offerNobody`.

item.name: D · Contract negotiation
item.description:
The consumer sends the offer back as a contract request; the provider checks the consumer's credentials against the policy.
Negotiation is asynchronous: the create call returns an id, then the state is polled.

request.description: Body = the offer from the catalog, unchanged, plus assigner (provider DID) and target (asset). Returns IdResponse with the negotiation id.
Returns {state}. Repeats until FINALIZED or TERMINATED (in the collection runner / newman).

item.name: E · Transfer and data access
item.description:
A pull transfer gives the consumer an EDR (endpoint + token). Data is read through the consumer's gateway, or directly from the provider's
public data plane with the token. Then the provider retires the agreement (access blocked) and reactivates it.

request.description: contractId = the consumer's agreement id. Returns IdResponse with the transfer process id.
Repeats until STARTED (the EDR has arrived).

The EDR: endpoint (provider public API), authType bearer, authorization (JWT signed with the provider key, audience = consumer).

item.description:
Locally nothing moves telemetry from Event Hub into storage, so we post one event per side of a contract, generate the
consumer's monthly report and download it with a JWT.

request.description: What the ingestion step would store for each record from the event broker. 201.

text/csv: contract_id, counterparty_name, data_transfer_response_status, total_transfer_size_in_kB, total_number_of_events. Authorization: Bearer <JWT with roles [Participant.consumer]> (built in the pre-request script).

exec: pm.test("our contract is in the report", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.include("postman-" + pm.collectionVariables.get("runId")));

item.name: 3 · Reference · Catalogs
item.description:
DSP catalog through the consumer's connector, a single dataset, the authority's federated catalog cache, and the
credential-filtered federated catalog.

request.description: DCAT Catalog: participantId, service (DSP endpoint), dataset[] each with hasPolicy (offer) and distribution (transfer types). The offer @id is base64(contract definition id):base64(asset id):base64(uuid).
One dataset by id.
The authority's cache (crawled every 10 s). Needs a JSON-LD QuerySpec; a bare {} is rejected. One catalog per crawled participant.
Property paths use the full JSON-LD IRI. Nested DCAT paths look like properties.'http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#theme'.'http://purl.org/dc/terms/identifier'.

item.name: Federated catalog · filtered for the consumer

request.description: DSE. The consumer's control plane calls the authority's catalog filter with a token; datasets whose RestrictedDiscoveryClaim fails are removed. Keys may come prefixed (dcat:dataset, dspace:participantId).
